To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) We introduce a model-based reinforcement learning objective based on mutual information maximization with variational empowerment that prioritizes information relevant to the task, and (2) We show experimentally on a suite of visual control tasks that this objective outperforms standard model-based RL approaches.

(a) we introduce an information prioritization objective that is based on variational empowerment and can be used for model-based reinforcement learning with visual observations; (b) this objective can be used in combination with mutual-information maximization to learn representations for visual model-based reinforcement learning without reconstruction; and (c) this objective leads to better sample efficiency and performance in visual model-based reinforcement tasks.

we propose a new objective for model-based reinforcement learning that allows for prioritization of functionally relevant information, which is important for visual model-based reinforcement learning, and that we show that the proposed approach outperforms state of the art approaches in terms of episodal return and sample efficiency.
